entries.source: my151 is smart, it knows that if you choose Bulbasaur, then Venusaur should join your dex too. my151 is smooth and easy to use, providing a "paint-by-numbers" template of Pokédex sections (like regional bird, Pikaclone, pseudo-legendary, and more), so you spend more time making thoughtful choices instead of trying to remember Pokémon. my151 also guides you towards making a balanced and realistic regional Pokédex, by providing detailed analytics into your dex's distribution of type, BST, and evolutionary stage, as well as comparisons to official regional Pokédexes.

Generation 1 introduced the original 151 Pokémon in the Kanto region. While later generations introduced anywhere from 72-156 new Pokémon, regional dexes usually included Pokémon from prior generations, landing them around 200-400 total. my151 encourages using 151 slots because that is the size that forces real choices, and the size most fans grew up with.
Free, in the browser, no sign-up, no download. Your dex saves in this browser and exports as a PNG.

Not yet, the picker covers the 1,025 official Pokémon. For a fakemon region, you can place stand-ins of official Pokémon with the same types for now: the sections and the type distribution still work. If you want us to support fakemon, please share that feedback with us so we can prioritize what to build next!

Yes. Export the Full grid, or choose Summary for your type, generation, starter, legendary, gimmick, and overall favorites. Both save as PNGs.
Free, in the browser, no sign-up, no download. Your choices save in this browser. Clearing browser data can remove them, so export a PNG to keep your chart.
Yes. The Pokédex builder and gym leader maker can filter their Pokémon lists to your saved favorites in this browser.
How do I make a favorite Pokémon chart by type and generation?

Can I export a chart of my favorite Pokémon of each type?
Is it free? Do I need an app or an account?
Can I use my favorites in the other my151 tools?
Yes. No account, no download. Everything saves in your browser (the webapp supports mobile, tablet, and desktop!) and exports as a PNG you can save or share anywhere.

The original Kanto Pokédex had 151 Pokémon. my151 encourages you to choose 151 Pokémon so you're forced to make meaningful tradeoffs, but the tool allows you to add as many Pokémon as you like in your ideal region.

Whatever is most fun for you! You can start with the Pokédex builder and choose gym leader teams out of the Pokémon in your region, or start with the gym leader maker and design your dex to include the Pokémon your trainers use.

Pick a type and signature Pokémon, then fill the team with evolution lines. The Pokémon automatically evolve according to when the leader would be encountered so early gyms face young forms and the Champion faces final ones, but you can adjust when the evolution line evolves.

my151 lets you design a gym leader's team across all encounter stages (no badges, eighth gym leader, endgame boss, etc.) - the original template is /vp/'s Pro Trainer Card, but my151 makes the template smooth and easy to fill all in one place, instead of requiring you to manually use an image editing app and find your own Pokémon sprites. my151 also lets you design several trainers and assemble them into a complete league, letting you see each trainer's team as you encounter them in the story, or with their full endgame rematch teams.

No. The card is the team, the badge and the type. There is no portrait or sprite maker. If you want us to support sprites or custom badges, please share that feedback with us so we can prioritize what to build next!

Your browser sends Global Privacy Control, so my151 never counts it.
my151 counts how people use it, so we can see what works and fix what does not. This page lists what we keep, why, and for how long. my151 has no ads and no accounts, and it sets no cookies.
The Pokémon in your Pokédex, your gym leader cards, and your favorite picks. We use them to count which Pokémon people choose.
Your browser's language, the app's language, your device type, and the names of your operating system and browser.
A random code in this browser's local storage. It links your visits together, so we count people, not page loads. It holds no name or contact details.
Your country, region, and time zone, which our host reads from your network address. We also note the local hour and weekday of your last visit.
Only its name, such as google.com, not the address of the page.

The text you send with Report a problem. It comes with the browser ID, your country, the page, the app version, your languages, your screen size, and your browser and system versions. If the app crashes, it sends the error details by itself.
When you visit, how long you stay active, and in which minutes. The pages you open, and steps such as finishing or downloading a build.
Each page load adds one to a daily count for that page, with no browser ID. When counting is off, the count notes that too, so we know how many visits we do not count.

Problem reports: no end date, but only the newest stay. That is 5,000 reports from browsers with a visit record, 1,000 from other browsers, and 1,000 crash reports.
Totals with no browser ID, such as daily visits or how many builds people downloaded: 400 days for daily totals, no end date for all-time totals.
